standing_doubles.why: no signature verification is performed: the claims are read out of the proof's own payload segment, unverified, so a scenario that authored a proof is answered with what it authored rather than with a forged validation
no crate in the federation dependency ceiling generates a uuid
session issuance is `mandate.identity`'s and reaches this crate as a port
client-administration authority is an authorization decision no crate in the federation ceiling makes
the relationship store is `story:graph-policy-adapter`'s
the policy engine is `story:graph-policy-adapter`'s

no audience registry is reachable from the authorization ceiling, so the caller states what it requires; this target requires what the context carries, which makes the audience bound satisfied rather than evaluated
no domain declares a mapping from an action to the roles that carry it, so the caller names the relation the graph is asked about
the revision floor a read must not answer below; the initial one, so a read is refused for the authority and never for the floor
the attribute input policy evaluates against; no declared command input carries one and no port answers it
the authority a request is made under; the declared input carries none, so no scope bound is intersected and none is claimed to have been
no crate in the authorization ceiling generates a uuid
an approval policy and a challenge expiry are values no port answers

delegation, revocation and agent-administration authority are authorization decisions (decision-blocker:guards) and the audience registry is mandate-token's; this target admits the verified subject and registers the context's audience, so a delegation command is refused for its records and never for an authority nobody evaluated
no crate in the authorization ceiling generates a uuid

no trust bundle is configured for a scenario and the SPIFFE verifier is story:agent-security's; this one verifies no proof, so AuthenticateWorkload is refused for its proof and never admitted on a forged verification
the in-memory double of the event-log adapter a later story supplies
the digest domain a deployment configures; this is the crate's own SHA-256
no crate in the STS dependency ceiling holds a random source
no crate in the STS dependency ceiling generates a uuid

UNMAPPED-ALGORITHM-POLICY: a SigningAlgorithm is a name and the admitted set is a deployment's, validated at startup; this target states one of the two names mandate-token admits so RegisterSigningKey is decided against a policy rather than against nothing
the longest lifetime a deployment issues an authorization code for; the contract carries no default and `code.rs` has no constant, so the ceiling IssueAuthorizationCode is bounded by is stated here

the signing key material is the deployment's and no scenario supplies one; the double signs under the `kid` of the key the scenario's own `SigningKey` records admit for issuance at the request's instant, and under a `kid` naming no record when they admit none, so the records, not the double, decide issuance
the public half of a key reference is material the deployment loads; this answers a thumbprint derived from the reference itself and computes no key

mandate.federation owns the OAuth client record and the STS reads it over an adapter no crate on this line supplies; this answers it from the scenario's federation fold, as the deployment's adapter answers it from the federation projection

mandate.identity owns the session record and the STS reads it over an adapter no crate on this line supplies; this answers it from the scenario's identity log, as the deployment's adapter answers it from the identity fold
the in-memory double of the code log the STS deployment supplies
